value.name: Asha returns to Pemberton Street
value.description: Asha drives back to Pemberton Street that afternoon to continue the investigation.
evidence: She drove back to Pemberton Street that afternoon.

value.name: Daniel has effectively moved in
value.description: Asha realizes Daniel is now staying at the house regularly, with his belongings and work setup taking over the space.
evidence: Daniel was there. Daniel was always there now, she realized. He had moved in, or as good as.
There was a duffel bag at the foot of the stairs and a laptop open on the dining table and the smell of takeout coffee in cups that were not the family's cups.

value.name: Daniel confronts Asha for not calling
value.description: Daniel sharply objects that Asha did not call before coming over.
evidence: He looked up sharply when she came in.

value.name: Asha apologizes and announces an update
value.description: Asha apologizes for not calling and says she has an update for Daniel and Lucia.
evidence: "I should have. I'm sorry. I have an update."

value.name: Lucia joins the conversation
value.description: Lucia comes downstairs after hearing the voices, while Rosa remains absent.
evidence: Lucia came down the stairs behind her, hearing the voices.
Rosa, Asha noted, did not appear.

value.name: Family shifts meeting to the parlor
value.description: They move the discussion to the parlor because Daniel has taken over the dining table as his office, and Asha notices Helena's abandoned belongings there.
evidence: They sat in the parlor this time, because the dining table was Daniel's office now.
The parlor was where Helena had spent her evenings.

There was an armchair near the window with a quilt thrown over the back and a side table with a pair of reading glasses still on it and a paperback face down, splayed open at a page Helena had not finished.
Asha tried not to look at the chair.

value.name: Asha reports the codicil was executed
value.description: Asha tells Daniel and Lucia that the codicil was signed, citing Pinsky's file and the September twelfth meeting with witnesses.
evidence: "I have notes from Pinsky's file confirming the meeting on September twelfth, the witnesses, and the fact that a codicil was signed."

value.name: Asha reveals Pinsky gave original to mother
value.description: Asha explains that Pinsky gave the original codicil to their mother and kept no copy in his file.
evidence: "Pinsky gave the original to your mother. He did not retain a copy in his file."

value.name: Daniel accuses Pinsky of malpractice
value.description: Daniel reacts to the revelation by calling the transfer of the original malpractice.
evidence: Daniel did not move. "He gave her the original."

value.name: Asha qualifies the legal significance
value.description: Asha pushes back, saying the act was unusual but not necessarily malpractice because it was done at the mother's request.
evidence: "It is unusual. It is not, by itself, malpractice. It was at her request."
